page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, its right side cut off by the scan edge. At the top, a line of text with Arabic words; below it the section heading and running text. A section ornament sits between the sections. At the foot, a signature on the left and an Arabic catchword at the right. No running head and no marginal notes are visible.

main_text.head: SECT. V.
De Accentibus.
main_text.p: Accentus nulla est nota apud Arabes; Re-gula tamen generalis est, quód Dissyllaba at-tollunt penultimam, ut [illegible, ~5 letters] ónfur: Poly-syllaba antepenultimam, ut [illegible, ~5 letters] jánfuro, nisi penultima producatur per [illegible, ~3 letters] quie-scentia, ut supra; tunc enim illa habet accen-tum, ut ilåhon, &c.
main_text.head: SECT. VI.
De radicalibus & servilibus literis.
main_text.p: Radix est tertia praeteriti persona singula-ris masculina, quæ literis nunquam constat paucioribus quàm tribus, ut [illegible, ~5 letters] juzit,

page.notes: The right edge of the scan cuts off the ends of most lines, so the line endings after "Dissyllaba", "accen-", "sunt," and "juzit," are incomplete. The Arabic words (top line, and in the text after "ut") are not legible enough to copy and are marked illegible. The Arabic catchword at the bottom right is partly cut off. The printed "Diffyllaba" and "fingula-ris" were read with long s as s; the printing may be a doubled f. The ornament between the sections and the section divider are not text.
